summary: Residency policy refresh race condition causing mixed-egress paths and regional latency bump
description:
Issue summary: Customer (AtlasMedia, Dedicated) reports intermittent increased p95/p99 latency and occasional cross-region egress after enabling 'residency_preference=strict' on their account. The behavior appears during policy refresh windows and correlates with bursty traffic from their ingestion workers.

Impact: Elevated p95/p99 for generation requests from eu-west users (~200-500ms delta) and occasional cross-region egress (requests routed from eu-west -> us-west) for short windows (~30-90s). Customer reports increased cost due to cross-region egress and user-facing latency spikes during peak times.

Environment: prod, Dedicated pool (atlas-dedicated-gpu-1), live since 2026-02-28.

Observed behavior: Requests normally route to eu-west serving nodes. During periodic policy refresh (~every 60s control-plane refresh), a subset of sessions are forwarded to us-west edges, causing TLS handshake and additional routing latency. This is intermittent and correlates with control-plane policy refresh timestamps seen in control-plane logs.

Expected behavior: With residency_preference=strict, traffic should remain pinned to eu-west and never egress to us-west unless explicit failover occurs or capacity is exhausted and fallback policy is triggered.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer sets residency_preference="strict" for tenant.
2) Send a steady stream of generation requests from eu-west clients (RPS ~40-60) with session affinity headers (X-Session-ID).
3) Observe routing in request trace and edge logs over 10 minutes.
4) Note any short windows where requests are routed to us-west and latency increases.

Expected: No cross-region hops when capacity is available in eu-west. Actual: transient cross-region egress coinciding with policy refresh cadence.
logs:
Control-plane log excerpt (2026-03-10T14:02:00Z): 
[control-plane] refresh_policy tenant=atlasmedia policy_version=18 start
[control-plane] compute_affinity_changes tenant=atlasmedia changed=27
[edge-eu-west] session_lookup id=snip-abc result=PIN_EXPIRED last_seen=2026-03-10T14:01:58Z
[edge-eu-west] forward_to=us-west host=gw-us-west-03 reason=fallthrough
[edge-us-west] accept_request session_hint=snip-abc

Request trace (sample): trace_id=tx-77bbc latency=780ms path=edge-eu-west -> gw-us-west TLS_handshake=220ms

Grafana alerts: increased p99 for atlasmedia eu-west generation route starting 14:02:10Z for ~70s.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: race between control-plane policy refresh and edge pin refresh leads to temporary TTL/pin inconsistencies. Two possible vectors: (1) control-plane computes a micro-migration (rebalancing) while edges still see old pin metadata, causing fallthrough to fallback route; (2) DNS TTL reduction on control-plane side during refresh causing some edges to re-resolve to secondary edge set.

What we've checked so far:
- Validated control-plane logs show policy_version increments at same cadence reported by customer.
- Edge metrics show pin_cache_miss spikes aligning with policy refresh window.
- No GPU shortage or autoscale events in dedicated pool during incidents.
- Session affinity header present in requests; edge reports last_seen < 60s but pin considered expired due to race condition.
- Reproduced locally with a synthetic load: when we trigger a policy refresh while simultaneously rotating edge routing table, ~5-8% of sessions fall through to fallback path for ~20-60s.

Correlated artifacts: Slack thread #support (https://slack.redwood/archives/C03SUP), Grafana panel (https://grafana.redwood/dashboard/routing?orgId=1&var-tenant=atlasmedia), and a debug PR with instrumentation (https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/908).

Hypothesis refinement: The control-plane publishes routing deltas and a short 'refresh-window' where edges accept both old and new pins to avoid hard-cutovers. In this window, our TTL/expiry logic on the edge treats pins as stale if last_seen < configured_pin_refresh_threshold, which combined with a small DNS re-resolve leads to mixed egress.

Next diagnostic step: add higher-fidelity tracing to pin state transitions and bump pin_refresh_grace to observe effect. Also evaluate candidate fix to debounce policy refresh broadcasts and add a short 'pin-hold' on edges during refresh to prevent fallthrough.
comments: 2026-03-10 15:05 - Support (Ava Martinez): Initial triage complete. Escalating to SRE/Routing. Asking customer for request IDs and sample traces.
2026-03-10 16:20 - Customer (AtlasMedia - Ops Lead, Jorge Ruiz): Provided three sample trace IDs and noted spikes only during 14:02-14:04 windows. Attached internal load generator plan.

2026-03-10 18:12 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Reproduced locally with synthetic load. Pin-cache miss spikes coincide with policy refresh broadcast. Raising priority and opening router PR for instrumentation. See PR #908.

2026-03-11 09:34 - Support (Ava Martinez): Shared interim workaround with customer: enable 'strict_no_failover' flag (controls application-level) to prevent automatic fallback while we test. Customer will trial on a subset of traffic.
2026-03-12 11:07 - Customer (Jorge Ruiz): Trial applied to 10% traffic. Early results: p99 spike occurrence reduced but not eliminated. Awaiting SRE countermeasure rollout.
2026-03-12 14:55 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Deployed temporary config change to increase pin_refresh_grace from 3s -> 30s on eu-west edges. Monitoring for reduction in mixed egress events.
resolution:
Workaround: Increased pin_refresh_grace on eu-west edges (temporary) and instructed customer to enable strict_no_failover for canary traffic. This reduced mixed-egress occurrences during the test window but did not fully eliminate them.

Planned permanent fix: Engineering to implement a debounce on control-plane policy broadcasts and implement a short 'pin-hold' period on edges where the existing pin is preferred for a grace window during version transitions. Add metrics for pin_state_transitions and add automated canary to validate behavior.

Follow-ups:
- Router team to land PR #908 (instrumentation) and follow-up PR for debounce (target 2026-03-24).
- SRE to run extended soak test for 48 hours post-merge.
- Support to coordinate with AtlasMedia to schedule a maintenance window for permanent rollout.

Status: In Progress. No final resolution yet; customer notified of workaround and planned timeline.
